lesson: Card #6 went 4W-2L for +$16.31 — our best day yet. The wins were all genuine current-form cases (Sevilla, Rennes, Anderlecht, West Ham); the losses were the two where we tried to be clever about pricing (Union Berlin backed against a Schalke side that suddenly scored three, and AZ's Over 2.5 undone when they were held 1-1 by the bottom side). Good reminder that even a strong process doesn't remove genuine upset risk — it just keeps the losses from compounding.

matches.analysis: FEATURED MATCH. West Brom sit top of the Championship, won their last two (including 1-0 away at Derby), and are unbeaten at home this season with the joint-best defensive record in the division. QPR are winless in two, held scoreless in back-to-back games, and arrive with a genuine injury crisis — Ilias Chair and Karamoko Dembélé both out, plus two defenders (Dunne, Lamptey) who limped off their last match and are doubtful. This is form, table position, and team news all pointing the same direction.

Ipswich have conceded 7 goals in their last two matches (5 at Old Trafford, 2 at home to Liverpool) and scored only twice. Palace's own form is mixed, but they showed they can score with a 3-2 comeback win at Fulham last time out. Model gives Palace a clear 50.5% to Ipswich's 24%.

Mainz just put 5 past Hamburg away from home — a genuine statement result. Frankfurt, meanwhile, are already on our tracker for the wrong reasons: they lost 1-4 at home to Augsburg in Card #1, and haven't shown much since. Model rates Mainz 53.7% at home to Frankfurt's 23.6%.

A more modest edge than the others on the card today, but a real one: Osasuna are the stronger side at home this season and Espanyol have been unremarkable on the road. Model gives Osasuna 41.3% to Espanyol's 28.6%, with the draw the next most likely outcome — standard conviction, not a marquee pick.

Two teams arriving in explosive form: Strasbourg just won 6-2 away at Troyes, and Monaco beat PSG 2-1 away from home. Picking a winner between two sides scoring (and conceding) this freely is guesswork; backing the goals is the cleaner read on the actual data.

A mild home edge on the model (42.9% to 28.6%) but nothing sharp enough to back with real conviction. Pass — Saturdays like today have dozens of fixtures across Europe, and not every one needs a stake.
